At lower thicknesses of coatings (i.e. 0.06 mm and 0.08 mm), an increase in the fatigue life was obtained in comparison with the alloy material without a coating. The specimens with coating thicknesses of 0.15 and 0.19 mm showed a lower number of cycles to failure in comparison with specimens without a coating.
